A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RethinkMCTS. All 11 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including v2's appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original APPS and HumanEval evaluations, component ablations, search-granularity comparisons, and rethink analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds controlled comparisons, reward-weight experiments, token-cost measurements, and repeated-run results.

M1.justification: Thought-level MCTS, block-level verbal feedback, leaf-thought refinement, and dual evaluation remain unchanged. The additional prompts and Algorithm 1 document the existing procedure without establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval and the same three APPS difficulty levels. The added experiments reuse this coverage; mathematical reasoning and tool use are discussed only as potential applications.

E2.justification: The six named external baselines remain. v2 adds Base(16) alongside Base(1), introduces a controlled variant replacing rethink with reflection, and adds ToT and PG-TD to the rollout comparison in Figure 5.

E3.justification: The main backbone models, 16-rollout budget, branching limit, and default reward weights remain. New experiments introduce controlled reflection substitution, alternative reward weights (1.0, 0.2) and (1.0, 1.0), and per-question token and monetary-cost measurements. These extend the evaluation design without establishing changes to the original data split.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled rethink-versus-reflection analysis, reward-weight sensitivity, token-cost analysis, and GPT-4o-mini component and search-granularity studies. The rollout comparison gains additional comparators. The self-evaluation versus generated-tests study is retained from v1 Table 2 as v2 Table 6.

E5.justification: v1 supplies point estimates without run-count or uncertainty reporting. v2 Appendix B and Table 7 report means and standard deviations across three runs with different seeds for RethinkMCTS, ToT, LATS, and PG-TD, while identifying the main results as single-run results.

E6.justification: RethinkMCTS's Table 1 scores remain unchanged, but ToT scores for both backbones and GPT-4o-mini PG-TD scores are revised. For example, ToT's GPT-3.5-turbo HumanEval entry changes from 84.15 to 76.22; the reason is not fully specified. Substantial new results cover Base(16), reflection, reward weights, costs, additional ablations, and repeated runs.

T1.justification: The P-UCB, exploration-weight, and piecewise reward equations retain their mathematical content. Visit-count notation changes, and procedural pseudocode is added, but neither version presents new theorems, proofs, or substantive formal derivations relative to the other.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and benchmark-superiority claim remain. v2 explicitly adds superior performance with lower token consumption relative to reflection, and its conclusion extends the proposed applicability to other reasoning domains.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning feedback-dependent generalization, selection of the thought to refine, and unexplored fine-tuning. It discusses token overhead and new experimental mechanisms. However, the reward-weight discussion claims poorer performance on both datasets despite Table 3 showing improvements on introductory and interview APPS problems.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C, and D add baseline implementation descriptions, explicit prompts, example traces and feedback, and pseudocode. Appendix B newly discloses temperature zero. Conversely, v1's explicit instruction to split APPS test cases evenly into public and private sets is omitted. The resource link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cited background on code agents, semantic reasoning, and tree search. It adds explicit grounding in natural-language planning for code generation through Wang et al. (2024b), semantic reasoning through Tang et al. (2023), and newer refinement work. The central search-and-refine novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. The narrative emphasizes rethink versus reflection, removes the standalone MCTS primer, relocates the generated-tests analysis, and introduces structured appendices, limitations, and ethics sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column report to a two-column layout. v2 adds a reflection-comparison diagram, redraws the framework illustration, revises chart arrangements and rollout displays, expands Table 1 with averages and additional rows, and introduces numerous experimental tables and prompt panels.

improvement.justification: The controlled reflection comparison, cost accounting, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, and explicit prompts substantially strengthen the evidence and reproducibility of the unchanged method. These address important gaps in v1's support for rethink and its implementation documentation. Unexplained baseline-score revisions, the omitted APPS split description, and overbroad reward-weight interpretation temper the gains, but the overall improvement remains substantial.
